clue.text: No-nonsense police raid follows riot, ignoring regulars

indicators.note: the raid word comes after the trimmed riot in the answer
dropping the evenly placed letters of riot leaves only its odd-placed ones

parts.note: a bust is slang for a police raid

explanation.surface: A tough police operation goes in after a riot breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: A robust approach is a sturdy, practical one, synonymous with a no-nonsense attitude.

clue.text: Artist steps around one for light

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

indicators.note: the steps word goes round the numeral, enclosing it

parts.note: dance steps make a dance
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A painter dances round someone in search of a source of illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiance is a glow or brightness, a synonym for the noun light.

clue.text: Match commentator?

parts.note: the match is a wedding, not a sporting fixture, and the one who makes remarks at it is the groom's chief attendant giving his speech

explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests football or cricket with a broadcaster calling the play; here it is a marriage, and the commentator is whoever speaks at the reception.
explanation.definitionFit: The groom's chief supporter traditionally delivers a speech of comment and anecdote at a wedding.

clue.text: Tug on a path to intercept ship's freeloaders?

indicators.note: the inner pieces cut into the two ship letters, catching them in between

parts.note: SS, steamship, prefixes a ship's name

indicators.note: in this down clue the tug word sits on top of the rest

parts.note: to tug is to tow
a way is a path

explanation.surface: A tugboat on a route catches up with passengers who never paid.
explanation.definitionFit: People hidden aboard a vessel to travel free are cheekily called freeloaders, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Note amends books seen in church

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is a note added to a letter
to amend is to alter

explanation.surface: A memo revises the hymnbooks found in the pews.
explanation.definitionFit: These are volumes of the Psalms used for worship, an example of books found in church.

clue.text: Alcohol providing morale in the theatre?

indicators.note: joins the two parts, with the theatre word coming first in the answer

parts.note: an operating theatre is where surgical work happens
spirit is morale, as in team spirit

explanation.surface: A drink keeps up the cast's morale backstage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests the stage; it is the operating theatre in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a denatured ethanol mixture used for cleaning skin, so it is a form of alcohol.

clue.text: Beats speed speaking without coming to a climax

parts.note: a lick is slang for speed, as in going at a fair lick

indicators.note: speaking is cut off after its start, never reaching its end, so only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Talk delivered quickly that never builds to a big finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To lick someone is informal for to defeat them, so licks is a synonym for beats.

clue.text: Art form mounting tacit or easy displays

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means the letters climb upwards, read from bottom to top
the run of letters is shown within the words tacit or easy

explanation.surface: An artistic style on show, whether understated or effortless.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexually explicit literature or pictures form a recognised genre, a kind of art form.

clue.text: Country garden linked with the Cornwall area

indicators.note: joins the two pieces side by side

parts.note: Cornwall lies in the South West of England, SW
Eden is the garden of Genesis

explanation.surface: A rural garden connected with England's far south-west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country garden' reads as a cottage garden; 'Country' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scandinavian kingdom is a nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: Ignored Conservative with elderly bore

parts.note: elderly means old
to bore a burden is to shoulder it

explanation.surface: A Tory put up with an old drip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a tedious person; it is the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a frosty brush-off is to snub them, an idiom for deliberately ignored.

clue.text: Shame of this person wrapped in shroud on getting busted

indicators.note: the self word is enclosed by the jumbled letters
being busted means broken, so shroud on is rearranged

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: Disgrace for someone wrapped in a burial cloth when the police raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting busted' scrambles SHROUDON into DSHONOUR, and 'wrapped in' sets I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgrace or loss of honour is a synonym for shame.

clue.text: Copy line seen in feature of roadworks

indicators.note: the line letter appears inside the roadworks object

parts.note: traffic cones are the familiar sight at roadworks

explanation.surface: A duplicate line painted at roadworks.
explanation.definitionFit: A genetically identical reproduction, or any exact duplicate, is a copy.

clue.text: Might this identify a Royal Marines troop?

definitions.text: Might this identify a Royal Marines troop?

parts.note: a band is a troop or group

explanation.surface: Asks how one might recognise a unit of marine commandos.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth band worn round the sleeve can show unit or role, so it might identify soldiers.

clue.text: Encourage popular part of church

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a spire is the tall pointed top of a church tower

explanation.surface: Urging on a well-liked section of the church building.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill someone with confidence or motivation is a synonym of encourage.

clue.text: Line dance music on game shows

indicators.note: the letters are on display within music on game

explanation.surface: A dance in a line appears during the music for a game show.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin American party dance is done in a single file, an example of a line dance.

clue.text: Try twice to get acclaim

indicators.note: the trial word is written two times in a row

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court

explanation.surface: Make two attempts to win praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like attempt; it is the judge's sense, hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: This parliamentary cry of approval is an expression of acclaim, a noun used as a call.

clue.text: Lulu's thirst absorbing doctor and the writer

indicators.note: the craving word soaks up the other letters inside it

parts.note: a thirst for something is a hunger for it
MD, Doctor of Medicine
the setter calls themself I

explanation.surface: A craving that takes in a medic and the author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lulu's' hides the definition in a name; the 's is a link meaning 'is'. A lulu is an outstanding thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for something remarkable or excellent of its kind.

clue.text: Torn about always being respectful

indicators.note: the torn word goes round the other

parts.note: rent is torn, past tense of rend
ever means always

explanation.surface: Constantly torn but still showing deference.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing deep, solemn regard is a synonym of respectful.

clue.text: Photographs fail to be entered in competitions

indicators.note: the failing word is put inside the competitions word

parts.note: cups are trophy competitions
to lose is to fail

explanation.surface: Pictures that don't make the cut when submitted to contests.
explanation.definitionFit: Shots taken from very near the subject are a kind of photographs.

clue.text: Back trouble in so stormy an affair

indicators.note: the trouble word is turned back to front

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

indicators.note: a stormy mix rearranges in so

explanation.surface: A back problem in a turbulent romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back trouble' reads as a bad spine; 'Back' reverses AIL, and 'stormy' turns IN SO into ISON.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret romantic relationship is a liaison, a synonym for an affair.

clue.text: King wearing small child's hat

indicators.note: the child has the king around them like a garment

parts.note: a mite is a small child; the 's is a link meaning 'is'
R abbreviates Rex, king

explanation.surface: A monarch wearing a little one's cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's tall pointed headdress is a kind of hat.

clue.text: Malign deal protecting University College

indicators.note: the deal word surrounds the college letters, shielding them

parts.note: to deal is to trade
UC abbreviates University College

explanation.surface: A shady agreement that shields a London college.
explanation.definitionFit: To slander or speak ill of someone is to traduce them, a synonym of malign as a verb.

clue.text: Music bars will need refurbished seats to muffle volume

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap round the volume letter, smothering it
refurbished means made over, so seats is rearranged

explanation.surface: Music venues need new seating to soften the noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refurbished' turns SEATS into STAES, and 'to muffle' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-line systems on which notes are written are what the clue calls music bars.

clue.text: Knocked sharply on front of this, cornered

indicators.note: in this across clue the knock word follows the single letter
takes just the opening letter of this

parts.note: rapped means knocked sharply

explanation.surface: Someone banged on this door, then found themselves boxed in.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught with no escape is a synonym for cornered.

clue.text: Fruit and veg needed by church

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A church harvest festival needs fruit and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft stone fruit is an example of fruit.

clue.text: Take off, seeing Italian grabbed by single pal

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the Italian letters are held inside the other two pieces

parts.note: a mate is a pal
IT abbreviates Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: Leave when you see an Italian seized by one friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests departing; it means doing an impression of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic or parody someone is to take them off, a synonym of imitate.

clue.text: Prospect of victory, as it falls

parts.note: V stands for victory, as in the V sign

indicators.note: letters that fall are tumbled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The chances of winning, as things stand when it collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospect of victory' reads as a chance of winning; 'falls' jumbles AS IT into ISTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A view or outlook over a landscape is a synonym of prospect.

clue.text: Drops measuring equipment

parts.note: drops looks like a verb meaning lets fall, but the drops are of water from the sky, and this kit measures them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops' reads as a verb, someone dropping gear; it is a plural noun for the falling water.
explanation.definitionFit: This meteorological instrument collects and measures falling precipitation.

clue.text: Stars head off for shelter

parts.note: suns are stars

indicators.note: off means awry, so the letters of head are rearranged

explanation.surface: Celebrities make for cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' reads as setting out; 'off' jumbles HEAD into HADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol or awning gives protection from the sun, a form of shelter.

clue.text: Enthusiastic study in painting

indicators.note: the study word sits inside the painting word

parts.note: painting is art
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Keen on studying painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate and fervent, a close synonym of enthusiastic.
